limits: Chapter says the architecture is 'validated at multiple companies' but gives no data.
Chapter says order of steps follows what the author commonly sees; needs differ per application.
Author notes it is unclear whether full or partial side-by-side responses give more reliable feedback.
Rating-option rewrites for Uber are 'not validated' (footnote).
Tool gateway not covered as not a common pattern as of writing.
practices: Start with the simplest architecture (query to model) and add components only as needs arise: context, guardrails, router/gateway, caches, agent patterns (Architecture intro).
Treat context construction like feature engineering for foundation models (Step 1).
Add input guardrails (PII masking with reverse map) and output guardrails (retry, parallel calls, human fallback); track false refusal rate too (Step 2).
Guardrails trade reliability against latency and work poorly in stream-completion mode (Guardrail implementation).
Use a small, fast intent classifier as router; adjust context when routing to models with smaller context limits (Step 3).
Put a model gateway in front of models for unified interface, access control, cost limits, fallback (Step 3).
Evaluate efficiency, cost and performance risk before adding a semantic cache; do not cache user-specific or time-sensitive queries (Step 4).
Make observability integral to design; track MTTD, MTTR and CFR (Monitoring).
Design metrics around the failure modes you want to catch; correlate metrics with north-star metrics (Metrics).
Log everything with tags and IDs; inspect production data manually each day (Logs and traces).
Trace each query step by step so the failing step can be pinpointed (Logs and traces).
Detect system prompt, user behaviour and underlying model drift (Drift detection).
Start without an orchestrator; judge orchestrators on integration/extensibility, complex pipelines, ease of use/performance/scalability (Orchestration).
Feed issues found in monitoring into the evaluation pipeline, and make evaluation metrics translate to monitoring metrics (Monitoring).
Collect feedback non-intrusively at the start, when something bad happens, and when the model has low confidence (Feedback Design).
Vary option positions or model position effects to mitigate position bias; inspect rating distributions for leniency bias (Feedback Limitations).
Be careful using feedback to train models: degenerate loops and sycophancy risk (Feedback Limitations).

terms.definition: mean time to detection: When something bad happens, how long does it take to detect it?
mean time to response: After detection, how long does it take to be resolved?
change failure rate: The percentage of changes or deployments that result in failures requiring fixes or rollbacks.
the whole process of instrumentating, tracking, and debugging the system (monitoring is the act of tracking a system's information)
cached items are used only when these exact items are requested
cached items are used even if they are only semantically similar, not identical, to the incoming query
an intermediate layer that allows your organization to interface with different models in a unified and secure manner
predictions themselves influence the feedback, which, in turn, influences the next iteration of the model, amplifying initial biases
explicit: info users provide in response to explicit requests; implicit: information inferred from user actions
